frokost.name: Breakfast
frokost.note: A Norwegian breakfast table usually has sliced bread. Cheese, jam and everything else put on bread is called pålegg.

kiosken.name: Kiosk and petrol station
kiosken.note: At a Norwegian kiosk a sausage comes in a bun (brød) or rolled in a thin potato flatbread (lompe). Drinks marked pant carry a bottle deposit, paid when you buy them.

butikken.name: Supermarket
butikken.note: Empty bottles and cans go into the supermarket's return machine (panteautomat). It prints a deposit slip you can use at the till.

matpakke.name: Packed lunch
matpakke.note: For school or work many people pack slices of bread with toppings in a lunch box, with a sheet of baking paper between them.

torget.name: Market
torget.note: In summer and autumn the market sells local berries; multer are cloudberries, golden yellow when ripe.

kafe.name: Café
kafe.note: In a Norwegian café a waffle often breaks into small heart-shaped pieces; you can have it with jam or sour cream.

17-mai.name: Constitution Day
17-mai.note: On 17 May people watch the children's parade and eat hot dogs and ice cream. A festive cake with strawberries, blueberries and cream is common too.

middag.name: Dinner at home
middag.note: Kokte poteter at a home dinner are boiled potatoes. Fish cakes and meatballs usually come with potatoes and vegetables.

bursdag.name: Birthday party
bursdag.note: A birthday table has cake and drinks. When the cake comes out, the guests say Gratulerer med dagen! (Happy birthday!)

hyttetur.name: Cabin and hiking
hyttetur.note: Before a hike from the cabin people fill a thermos with hot cocoa and bring oranges and chocolate; back at the cabin there is a bowl of hot soup.

grillfest.name: Barbecue party
grillfest.note: In summer Norwegians move the grill outdoors. Corn, fish and vegetables are grilled along with the meat, and potato salad is a usual side.

bakedag.name: Baking day
bakedag.note: Norwegian recipes measure volume in dl (decilitres) and l (litres) and weight in g (grams). ss is a tablespoon and ts a teaspoon, the standard measuring spoons in recipes.

fredagstaco.name: Friday taco
fredagstaco.note: Many Norwegian families have tacos on Friday: bowls of fillings go on the table and everyone builds their own.

verden.name: The world on a plate
verden.note: Norwegian menus often have dishes from other food traditions, such as sushi, lasagne, kebab and curry. Recognising the ingredients on the menu makes ordering much easier.

julebord.name: Christmas dinner
julebord.note: Many families eat crispy pork ribs (ribbe) or cured lamb ribs (pinnekjøtt) at Christmas; the sides vary by family and region. The rice pudding riskrem usually comes with red berry sauce.

restaurant.name: Three-course restaurant
restaurant.note: At a restaurant forrett is the starter, hovedrett the main course and dessert the dessert. You can mention allergies when ordering, for example "Jeg er allergisk mot nøtter." (I'm allergic to nuts.)
